The width of the 90% confidence intervals directly reflects the increasing uncertainty associated with longer time horizons. While these intervals capture a wide range of plausible outcomes, certain specific risks or events could push the actual value beyond these bounds. These "black swan" type events or highly impactful surprises are by definition difficult to predict and are the primary factors that could lead to outcomes outside the forecasted ranges.
